ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, ABCD is a square with a side length of 4. Point E is on the diagonal BD, and $ \angle BAE=22.5^\circ$, $EF\perp AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular at F. What is the length of EF?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In the square $ABCD$, $\angle ABD = \angle ADB = 45^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle BAE = 22.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAE = 90^\circ - \angle BAE = 67.5^\circ$.\\
In $\triangle ADE$, $\angle AED = 180^\circ - 45^\circ - 67.5^\circ = 67.5^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAE = \angle ADE$.\\
$\therefore AD = DE = 4$.\\
$\because$ The side length of the square is 4,\\
$\therefore BD = 4\sqrt{2}$.\\
$\therefore BE = BD - DE = 4\sqrt{2} - 4$.\\
$\because EF \perp AB, \angle ABD = 45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BEF$ is an isosceles right triangle.\\
$\therefore EF = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}BE = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \times (4\sqrt{2} - 4) = \boxed{4 - 2\sqrt{2}}$.
